metadata.description: A Unique name used for the Virtual Machine domain and also for generating resource names. Defaults to a value prefixed with "aiovm-".
Type of authentication to use on the Virtual Machine. SSH key is recommended.
SSH key or password for the Virtual Machine. SSH key is recommended.
The size of the VM, at least 16GB RAM is required

variables.$fxv#0:
#cloud-config

# Note: This script assumes an Ubuntu 22.04 (Jammy) base image
# Ensure the VM has System-Assigned Managed Identity enabled
# before deploying this cloud-config.

write_files:
  # 1. Initial MOTD
  - path: /etc/motd
    owner: root:root
    permissions: '0644'
    content: |
      +------------------------------------------------------------+
      |          Azure IoT Operations Dev VM Provisioning          |
      +------------------------------------------------------------+
      | Status: Waiting to start...                                |
      | Script will start after boot completes                     |
      |                                                            |
      | If setup doesn't start automatically:                      |
      | $ sudo bash /root/provision_ops_vm.sh                      |
      |                                                            |
      | To watch progress in real-time:                            |
      | $ watch cat /etc/motd                                      |
      | Or view full logs:                                         |
      | $ sudo tail -f /var/log/aio-provision.log                  |
      | Or check service status:                                   |
      | $ sudo systemctl status aio-provision.service              |
      | $ journalctl -u aio-provision.service -f                   |
      +------------------------------------------------------------+

  # 2. Azure CLI Sources File - Uses Jammy (Ubuntu 22.04)
  - path: /etc/apt/sources.list.d/azure-cli.list
    owner: root:root
    permissions: '0644'
    content: |
      deb [arch=amd64 signed-by=/etc/apt/keyrings/microsoft.gpg] https://packages.microsoft.com/repos/azure-cli/ jammy main

  # 3. k9s Configuration File - Pre-created for root and user
  - path: /root/.k9s/config.yml
    owner: root:root
    permissions: '0644'
    content: |
      k9s:
        refreshRate: 2
        headless: false
        readOnly: false
        noIcons: false
        logger:
          tail: 100
          buffer: 5000
          sinceSeconds: 60
          fullScreenLogs: false
          textWrap: false
          showTime: false

  # 4. Improved provisioning script (HTML tags removed)
  - path: /root/provision_ops_vm.sh
    owner: root:root
    permissions: '0700'
    content: |
      #!/bin/bash

      # Enable error handling
      set -e

      # Set non-interactive mode for apt
      export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

      # Set up logging
      LOG_FILE="/var/log/aio-provision.log"
      exec > >(tee -a ${LOG_FILE}) 2>&1

      echo "========================================================"
      echo "Starting Azure IoT Operations provisioning at $(date)"
      echo "Log file: ${LOG_FILE}"
      echo "========================================================"

      # Total number of steps
      TOTAL_STEPS=12

      # Function to update status in MOTD
      update_status() {
        local step_num="$1"
        local status_msg="$2"
        shift 2
        local details=("$@")

        {
          echo "+------------------------------------------------------------+"
          echo "|          Azure IoT Operations Dev VM Provisioning          |"
          echo "+------------------------------------------------------------+"
          printf "| Status: Step %s of %s - %-35s |\n" "$step_num" "$TOTAL_STEPS" "$status_msg"
          echo "|                                                            |"

          for detail in "${details[@]}"; do
            printf "| %-58s |\n" "$detail"
          done

          # Pad with empty lines if fewer details than expected
          local num_details=${#details[@]}
          for (( i=$num_details; i<6; i++ )); do
              echo "|                                                            |"
          done

          echo "| To watch progress: $ watch cat /etc/motd                   |"
          echo "| View full logs:  $ sudo tail -f $LOG_FILE                |"
          echo "+------------------------------------------------------------+"
        } > /etc/motd
      }

      # Function to set final status in MOTD
      final_status() {
        local status="$1"
        local msg="$2"
        shift 2
        local details=("$@")

        {
          echo "+------------------------------------------------------------+"
          echo "|          Azure IoT Operations Dev VM Provisioning          |"
          echo "+------------------------------------------------------------+"
          printf "| Status: %-50s |\n" "$status"
          printf "| %-58s |\n" "$msg"
          echo "|                                                            |"

          for detail in "${details[@]}"; do
             printf "| %-58s |\n" "$detail"
          done

           # Pad with empty lines if fewer details than expected
          local num_details=${#details[@]}
          for (( i=$num_details; i<10; i++ )); do
              echo "|                                                            |"
          done

          echo "+------------------------------------------------------------+"
        } > /etc/motd
         # Also log final status
        echo "================== FINAL STATUS: $status =================="
        echo "$msg"
        for detail in "${details[@]}"; do echo "- $detail"; done
        echo "========================================================"
      }

      # --- Provisioning Steps ---

      ##### Step 1: Set up repositories #####
      update_status "1" "Setting up repositories" \
        "Adding package sources..."

      # Ensure keyring directory exists
      mkdir -p -m 755 /etc/apt/keyrings

      echo "Adding Microsoft repository for Ubuntu 22.04 (Jammy)..."
      # Uses the key already fetched by runcmd (/etc/apt/keyrings/microsoft.gpg)
      wget -q https://packages.microsoft.com/config/ubuntu/22.04/packages-microsoft-prod.deb -O packages-microsoft-prod.deb
      dpkg -i packages-microsoft-prod.deb
      rm packages-microsoft-prod.deb

      echo "Adding Kubernetes repository (v1.30)..." # Adjust version if needed
      K8S_APT_VERSION="v1.30"
      curl -fsSL "https://pkgs.k8s.io/core:/stable:/${K8S_APT_VERSION}/deb/Release.key" | gpg --dearmor -o /etc/apt/keyrings/kubernetes-apt-keyring.gpg
      chmod 644 /etc/apt/keyrings/kubernetes-apt-keyring.gpg
      echo "deb [signed-by=/etc/apt/keyrings/kubernetes-apt-keyring.gpg] https://pkgs.k8s.io/core:/stable:/${K8S_APT_VERSION}/deb/ /" | tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/kubernetes.list > /dev/null

      ##### Step 2: Install packages #####
      update_status "2" "Installing packages" \
        "Waiting for package manager lock..." \
        "Track details: sudo tail -f $LOG_FILE"

      echo "Waiting for apt locks to be released..."
      while fuser /var/lib/dpkg/lock >/dev/null 2>&1 || fuser /var/lib/apt/lists/lock >/dev/null 2>&1 || fuser /var/cache/apt/archives/lock >/dev/null 2>&1; do
        echo "Waiting for locks..."
        sleep 5
      done

      echo "Updating package lists..."
      update_status "2" "Updating package lists" \
         "Running apt-get update..."
      apt-get update -y || { echo "WARNING: First apt-get update failed, retrying..."; sleep 10; apt-get update -y; }

      update_status "2" "Installing packages" \
        "Installing: Docker, Azure CLI, kubectl, Helm, k3d, k9s, utils" \
        "This may take several minutes..." \
        "Track details: sudo tail -f $LOG_FILE"

      # Install base packages and prerequisites
      echo "Installing prerequisites and utilities..."
      apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
        apt-transport-https \
        ca-certificates \
        curl \
        gnupg \
        lsb-release \
        jq \
        git \
        wget || { echo "WARNING: Failed to install base utils, retrying..."; sleep 10; apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends apt-transport-https ca-certificates curl gnupg lsb-release jq git wget; }

      # Check & Install Docker
      if ! command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        echo "Installing Docker..."
        apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends docker.io || { echo "WARNING: Failed to install docker.io, retrying..."; sleep 10; apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends docker.io; }
      else
        echo "Docker already installed."
      fi

      # Check & Install Azure CLI (relies on sources.list and key from cloud-init)
      if ! command -v az >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        echo "Installing Azure CLI..."
        apt-get install -y azure-cli || { echo "WARNING: Failed to install azure-cli, retrying..."; sleep 10; apt-get install -y azure-cli; }
      else
        echo "Azure CLI already installed."
      fi

      # Check & Install kubectl
      if ! command -v kubectl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        echo "Installing kubectl..."
        apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends kubectl || { echo "WARNING: Failed to install kubectl, retrying..."; sleep 10; apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends kubectl; }
      else
        echo "kubectl already installed."
      fi

      # Clean up apt cache
      echo "Cleaning apt cache..."
      apt-get clean

      ##### Step 3: Ensure Docker is running #####
      update_status "3" "Starting Docker service" \
        "Ensuring Docker daemon is running and ready..."

      echo "Enabling and starting Docker service..."
      systemctl enable docker
      systemctl start docker

      echo "Waiting for Docker daemon to be ready..."
      for i in $(seq 1 30); do
        if docker info >/dev/null 2>&1; then
          echo "Docker is ready!"
          break
        fi
        if [ $i -eq 30 ]; then
          echo "ERROR: Docker failed to start properly after 30 seconds"
          final_status "FAILED" "Docker service failed to start" \
            "Check Docker status: sudo systemctl status docker" \
            "See logs: journalctl -u docker"
          exit 1
        fi
        echo "Waiting for Docker ($i/30)..."
        sleep 2 # Increased sleep slightly
      done

      ##### Step 4: Install K3d & K9s #####
      update_status "4" "Installing K3d" \
        "Downloading and installing K3d..."

      if ! command -v k3d >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        echo "Installing k3d..."
        curl -s https://raw.githubusercontent.com/k3d-io/k3d/main/install.sh | bash
        if ! command -v k3d >/dev/null 2>&1; then
          echo "ERROR: k3d installation failed"
          final_status "FAILED" "Failed to install K3d" \
            "Check logs: $LOG_FILE"
          exit 1
        fi
        echo "k3d installed successfully."
      else
        echo "k3d already installed."
      fi

      update_status "4" "Installing K9s" \
        "Downloading K9s Kubernetes UI..." \
        "Using GitHub API to find latest version"

      if ! command -v k9s >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        # Corrected: Use jq -r and sed to get version number
        K9S_VERSION=$(curl -s https://api.github.com/repos/derailed/k9s/releases/latest | jq -r .tag_name | sed 's/v//')
        if [ -z "$K9S_VERSION" ]; then
            echo "WARNING: Could not determine latest k9s version via GitHub API. Using fallback v0.32.4"
            K9S_VERSION="0.32.4" # Update this fallback periodically
        fi
        echo "Installing k9s version $K9S_VERSION..."
        # Corrected: Ensure tar extracts only k9s binary to /tmp
        curl -sL "https://github.com/derailed/k9s/releases/download/v${K9S_VERSION}/k9s_Linux_amd64.tar.gz" | tar xz -C /tmp k9s
        mv /tmp/k9s /usr/local/bin/
        chmod +x /usr/local/bin/k9s
        if ! command -v k9s >/dev/null 2>&1; then
           echo "WARNING: k9s installation appears to have failed, but continuing setup."
        else
           echo "k9s installed successfully!"
        fi
      else
        echo "k9s already installed."
      fi

      # Set up basic user environment (assuming user ID 1000 is the primary user)
      MYUSER=$(id -un 1000 || echo "user") # Fallback user if 1000 doesn't exist
      MYHOME=$(eval echo ~$MYUSER)
      MYWORK="/workspaces" # Define workspace dir

      # Create k9s config for the user
      if [ -d "$MYHOME" ]; then
        mkdir -p "$MYHOME/.k9s"
        cp /root/.k9s/config.yml "$MYHOME/.k9s/"
        chown -R "$MYUSER:$MYUSER" "$MYHOME/.k9s"
      fi

      ##### Step 5: Install Helm #####
      update_status "5" "Installing Helm" \
        "Downloading and installing Helm..."

      if ! command -v helm >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        echo "Installing Helm..."
        curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/helm/helm/main/scripts/get-helm-3 | bash
         if ! command -v helm >/dev/null 2>&1; then
          echo "ERROR: Helm installation failed"
          final_status "FAILED" "Failed to install Helm" \
            "Check logs: $LOG_FILE"
          exit 1
        fi
         echo "Helm installed successfully."
      else
        echo "Helm already installed."
      fi

      ##### Step 6: Configure environment and detect Azure resources #####
      update_status "6" "Detecting Azure resources" \
        "Querying Azure Instance Metadata Service (IMDS)..." \
        "Logging into Azure CLI using Managed Identity..."

      echo "Getting VM metadata from IMDS..."
      VM_METADATA=$(curl -s -H Metadata:true --noproxy "*" "http://169.254.169.254/metadata/instance?api-version=2021-02-01")

      if [ -z "$VM_METADATA" ]; then
        echo "ERROR: Failed to retrieve VM metadata from IMDS (http://169.254.169.254)"
        final_status "FAILED" "Could not retrieve VM metadata" \
          "Ensure VM can reach IMDS & has Managed Identity enabled."
        exit 1
      fi

      # Extract details
      export SUBSCRIPTION_ID=$(echo "$VM_METADATA" | jq -r '.compute.subscriptionId')
      export RESOURCE_GROUP=$(echo "$VM_METADATA" | jq -r '.compute.resourceGroupName')
      export LOCATION=$(echo "$VM_METADATA" | jq -r '.compute.location')
      export VM_NAME=$(echo "$VM_METADATA" | jq -r '.compute.name')
      export RESOURCE_NAME="${VM_NAME}-k8s" # Name for Arc-connected cluster resource

      echo "Logging into Azure with System-Assigned Managed Identity..."
      az login --identity > /dev/null || {
          echo "ERROR: Failed to login to Azure using Managed Identity."
          final_status "FAILED" "Azure login failed (Managed Identity)" \
            "Ensure System-Assigned Managed Identity is enabled on VM."
          exit 1
      }
      echo "Azure login successful."

      # Get VM Principal ID (needed for role assignments)
      echo "Retrieving VM Managed Identity Principal ID..."
      VM_PRINCIPAL_ID=$(az vm identity show --resource-group "$RESOURCE_GROUP" --name "$VM_NAME" --query principalId -o tsv 2>/dev/null)

      if [ -z "$VM_PRINCIPAL_ID" ]; then
        echo "ERROR: Could not retrieve VM Managed Identity Principal ID."
        final_status "FAILED" "Failed to get VM Principal ID" \
          "Ensure System-Assigned Managed Identity is enabled." \
          "Check 'az vm identity show' command manually."
         exit 1
      fi
      echo "VM Principal ID: $VM_PRINCIPAL_ID"

      update_status "6" "Detected Azure environment" \
        "Subscription: $SUBSCRIPTION_ID" \
        "Resource Group: $RESOURCE_GROUP" \
        "Location:       $LOCATION" \
        "VM Name:        $VM_NAME" \
        "Arc K8s Name:   $RESOURCE_NAME" \
        "VM PrincipalID: $VM_PRINCIPAL_ID"


      ##### Step 7: Create K3d cluster #####
      update_status "7" "Creating K3d cluster" \
        "Cluster name: k3s-default" \
        "Exposing ports: 1883, 8883, 8884" \
        "Creating local registry: k3d-registry.localhost:5000" \
        "This may take a few minutes..." \
        "Track details: sudo tail -f $LOG_FILE"

      CLUSTER_RECREATED=false
      if k3d cluster list 2>/dev/null | grep -q k3s-default; then
        echo "K3d cluster 'k3s-default' already exists."
        # Simple check: Can we get kubeconfig?
        if k3d kubeconfig get k3s-default > /dev/null 2>&1; then
          echo "Existing k3d cluster seems functional. Skipping recreation."
        else
          echo "Existing k3d cluster found but might have issues. Deleting..."
          k3d cluster delete k3s-default
          CLUSTER_RECREATED=true
        fi
      else
         CLUSTER_RECREATED=true
      fi

      if [ "$CLUSTER_RECREATED" = true ]; then
        echo "Creating K3d cluster 'k3s-default'..."
        k3d cluster create k3s-default \
          -p '1883:1883@loadbalancer' \
          -p '8883:8883@loadbalancer' \
          -p '8884:8884@loadbalancer' \
          --registry-create k3d-registry.localhost:127.0.0.1:5000 \
          --wait || {
            echo "ERROR: Failed to create K3d cluster 'k3s-default'"
            final_status "FAILED" "Failed to create K3d cluster" \
              "Check k3d logs or docker logs for k3d-k3s-default-server-0" \
              "Check logs: $LOG_FILE"
            exit 1
          }
         echo "K3d cluster created successfully."
      fi

      ##### Step 8: Configure kubectl #####
      update_status "8" "Configuring kubectl" \
        "Setting up kubeconfig for root and user ($MYUSER)" \
        "Testing cluster connection..." \
        "Run 'k9s' to monitor cluster"

      echo "Creating kubeconfig files..."
      mkdir -p /root/.kube
      k3d kubeconfig get k3s-default > /root/.kube/config
      chmod 600 /root/.kube/config

      if [ -d "$MYHOME" ]; then
        mkdir -p "$MYHOME/.kube"
        k3d kubeconfig get k3s-default > "$MYHOME/.kube/config"
        chown -R "$MYUSER:$MYUSER" "$MYHOME/.kube"
        chmod 600 "$MYHOME/.kube/config"
      fi

      echo "Verifying kubectl connection..."
      kubectl get nodes || {
        echo "ERROR: kubectl cannot connect to the cluster."
        final_status "FAILED" "kubectl configuration failed" \
          "Could not connect to k3d cluster via kubectl." \
          "Check k3d cluster status and kubeconfig files." \
          "Check logs: $LOG_FILE"
        exit 1
      }
      echo "kubectl connection verified."

      # Add k9s alias to bashrc if not present
      echo "Setting up k9s alias in .bashrc..."
      if ! grep -q "alias k9s=" /root/.bashrc; then
        echo 'alias k9s="KUBECONFIG=$HOME/.kube/config k9s"' >> /root/.bashrc
      fi
      if [ -d "$MYHOME" ] && ! grep -q "alias k9s=" "$MYHOME/.bashrc"; then
        echo 'alias k9s="KUBECONFIG=$HOME/.kube/config k9s"' >> "$MYHOME/.bashrc"
        chown "$MYUSER:$MYUSER" "$MYHOME/.bashrc"
      fi

      # Test k9s connection (best effort)
      echo "Testing k9s connection (headless)..."
       if command -v k9s >/dev/null 2>&1; then
         KUBECONFIG=/root/.kube/config k9s info --headless > /dev/null || {
            echo "WARNING: k9s command failed or couldn't connect to the cluster. Setup will continue."
         }
       else
         echo "WARNING: k9s command not found, skipping connection test."
       fi


      ##### Step 9: Connect K8s to Arc #####
      update_status "9" "Connecting to Azure Arc" \
        "Resource Name:  $RESOURCE_NAME" \
        "Resource Group: $RESOURCE_GROUP" \
        "Location:       $LOCATION" \
        "Installing/updating connectedk8s extension..." \
        "This may take several minutes..." \
        "Track details: sudo tail -f $LOG_FILE"

      echo "Adding/Updating Azure CLI extension: connectedk8s..."
      az extension add --upgrade --name connectedk8s --yes

      echo "Checking if cluster '$RESOURCE_NAME' is already connected to Arc..."
      ARC_CONNECTED=$(az connectedk8s show --name "$RESOURCE_NAME" --resource-group "$RESOURCE_GROUP" --query name -o tsv 2>/dev/null)

      if [ -z "$ARC_CONNECTED" ]; then
        echo "Connecting Kubernetes cluster '$RESOURCE_NAME' to Azure Arc..."
        az connectedk8s connect \
          --name "$RESOURCE_NAME" \
          --resource-group "$RESOURCE_GROUP" \
          --location "$LOCATION" || {
            echo "ERROR: Failed to connect Kubernetes cluster to Azure Arc."
            final_status "FAILED" "Failed to connect to Azure Arc" \
              "Check 'az connectedk8s connect' command output." \
              "Ensure managed identity has needed permissions if applicable." \
              "Check logs: $LOG_FILE"
            exit 1
          }
        echo "Successfully connected cluster to Azure Arc as '$RESOURCE_NAME'."
      else
        echo "Cluster '$RESOURCE_NAME' is already connected to Azure Arc. Skipping."
      fi

      ##### Step 10: Create Storage Account, Assign Permissions, Create Schema Registry #####
      # Generate unique storage account name (lowercase letters/numbers, 3-24 chars)
      UNIQUE_HASH=$(echo "$VM_NAME-$SUBSCRIPTION_ID" | md5sum | head -c 8)
      STORAGE_ACCOUNT="stiot$(echo $VM_NAME | head -c 8)${UNIQUE_HASH}" # Make more unique
      STORAGE_ACCOUNT=$(echo "$STORAGE_ACCOUNT" | tr -dc 'a-z0-9' | head -c 24) # Ensure compliance
      STORAGE_ACCOUNT=$(echo "$STORAGE_ACCOUNT" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')

      update_status "10" "Creating Azure Storage Account" \
        "Account Name:   $STORAGE_ACCOUNT" \
        "Resource Group: $RESOURCE_GROUP" \
        "Location:       $LOCATION" \
        "SKU:            Standard_LRS, Hierarchical Namespace: true" \
        "Track details: sudo tail -f $LOG_FILE"

      echo "Checking if storage account '$STORAGE_ACCOUNT' exists..."
      SA_ID=$(az storage account show --name "$STORAGE_ACCOUNT" --resource-group "$RESOURCE_GROUP" --query id -o tsv 2>/dev/null)

      if [ -z "$SA_ID" ]; then
        echo "Creating storage account '$STORAGE_ACCOUNT'..."
        az storage account create \
          --name "$STORAGE_ACCOUNT" \
          --resource-group "$RESOURCE_GROUP" \
          --location "$LOCATION" \
          --enable-hierarchical-namespace true \
          --sku Standard_LRS || {
            echo "ERROR: Failed to create storage account '$STORAGE_ACCOUNT'."
            final_status "FAILED" "Failed to create storage account" \
              "Check Azure quotas and naming rules." \
              "Check logs: $LOG_FILE"
            exit 1
          }
        SA_ID=$(az storage account show --name "$STORAGE_ACCOUNT" --resource-group "$RESOURCE_GROUP" --query id -o tsv)
        echo "Storage account created successfully. ID: $SA_ID"
      else
        echo "Storage account '$STORAGE_ACCOUNT' already exists. ID: $SA_ID"
      fi

      update_status "10" "Assigning Storage Permissions" \
        "Assigning roles to VM Managed Identity ($VM_PRINCIPAL_ID)" \
        "Roles: Storage Blob Data Owner, Owner (on Storage Account)" \
        "Scope: Storage Account ($STORAGE_ACCOUNT)" \
        "Waiting for Azure propagation..." \
        "Track details: sudo tail -f $LOG_FILE"

      echo "Waiting 60 seconds before assigning roles for propagation..."
      sleep 60

      # Define roles to assign
      # Note: 'Owner' is broad, used here for simplicity in dev setup.
      # 'Storage Blob Data Owner' is required for AIO operations.
      ROLES_TO_ASSIGN=("Storage Blob Data Owner" "Owner")
      ASSIGNMENT_SUCCESS=true
      OVERALL_ASSIGNMENT_STATUS=true # Track if any role failed

      for role in "${ROLES_TO_ASSIGN[@]}"; do
        echo "Attempting to assign role '$role'..."
        ASSIGNMENT_SUCCESS=false # Assume failure for this role initially
        for attempt in {1..3}; do
          # Check if assignment already exists
          if az role assignment list --assignee "$VM_PRINCIPAL_ID" --scope "$SA_ID" --role "$role" --query "[].id" -o tsv | grep -q "."; then
             echo "Role '$role' already assigned."
             ASSIGNMENT_SUCCESS=true # Mark as success
             break # Role exists, move to next role
          fi

          # Attempt assignment
          echo "Attempt $attempt: Assigning role '$role' to $VM_PRINCIPAL_ID on scope $SA_ID"
          if az role assignment create \
            --assignee-object-id "$VM_PRINCIPAL_ID" \
            --assignee-principal-type ServicePrincipal \
            --role "$role" \
            --scope "$SA_ID" > /dev/null; then # Suppress output on success
             echo "Successfully assigned role '$role'."
             ASSIGNMENT_SUCCESS=true # Mark as success
             break # Success, move to next role
          fi

          # Failed, wait and retry
          if [ $attempt -lt 3 ]; then
            echo "Failed attempt $attempt to assign role '$role'. Retrying in 30 seconds..."
            sleep 30
          else
            echo "ERROR: Failed to assign role '$role' after 3 attempts."
            # Do not exit here, just record the failure
          fi
        done

         if ! $ASSIGNMENT_SUCCESS; then
            OVERALL_ASSIGNMENT_STATUS=false # Mark that at least one role assignment failed
           # Decide how critical this failure is. For AIO, Blob Data Owner is critical.
           if [[ "$role" == "Storage Blob Data Owner" ]]; then
                final_status "FAILED" "Critical role assignment failed" \
                    "Failed to assign '$role'. Check Permissions/Logs." \
                    "Log file: $LOG_FILE"
                exit 1
           else
                echo "WARNING: Failed to assign non-critical role '$role'. Continuing..."
           fi
         fi
      done

      if ! $OVERALL_ASSIGNMENT_STATUS; then
          echo "WARNING: One or more role assignments failed or timed out. Setup continues, but some operations might require manual permission adjustments."
      else
          echo "Required role assignments completed or already existed."
      fi


      # Create Schema Registry
      # Generate unique schema registry name
      SCHEMA_REGISTRY="sriot$(echo $VM_NAME | head -c 8)${UNIQUE_HASH}"
      SCHEMA_REGISTRY=$(echo "$SCHEMA_REGISTRY" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]' | head -c 24)

      update_status "10" "Creating Azure Schema Registry" \
        "Name:           $SCHEMA_REGISTRY" \
        "Resource Group: $RESOURCE_GROUP" \
        "Namespace:      default" \
        "Storage Acct:   $STORAGE_ACCOUNT" \
        "Installing/updating azure-iot-ops extension..."

      echo "Adding/Updating Azure CLI extension: azure-iot-ops..."
      az extension add --upgrade --name azure-iot-ops --yes

      echo "Checking if schema registry '$SCHEMA_REGISTRY' exists..."
      SCHEMA_REG_EXISTS=$(az iot ops schema registry show --name "$SCHEMA_REGISTRY" --resource-group "$RESOURCE_GROUP" --query name -o tsv 2>/dev/null)

      if [ -z "$SCHEMA_REG_EXISTS" ]; then
        echo "Creating schema registry '$SCHEMA_REGISTRY'..."
        az iot ops schema registry create \
          --name "$SCHEMA_REGISTRY" \
          --resource-group "$RESOURCE_GROUP" \
          --registry-namespace "default" \
          --sa-resource-id "$SA_ID" || {
            echo "ERROR: Failed to create schema registry '$SCHEMA_REGISTRY'."
            final_status "FAILED" "Failed to create schema registry" \
              "Check prerequisite role assignments ('Storage Blob Data Owner')." \
              "Check logs: $LOG_FILE"
            exit 1
          }
         echo "Schema registry '$SCHEMA_REGISTRY' created successfully."
      else
        echo "Schema registry '$SCHEMA_REGISTRY' already exists. Skipping creation."
      fi

      ##### Step 11: Initialize IoT Operations #####
      update_status "11" "Initializing IoT Operations" \
        "Command: az iot ops init" \
        "Target Cluster: $RESOURCE_NAME (Arc)" \
        "Resource Group: $RESOURCE_GROUP" \
        "This deploys AIO CRDs and operator pods..." \
        "This may take up to 10 minutes..." \
        "Track cluster state with: k9s"

      # Check if already initialized by looking for the namespace
      echo "Checking if Azure IoT Operations namespace exists..."
      IOT_OPS_INITIALIZED=$(kubectl get ns azure-iot-operations --ignore-not-found)

      if [ -z "$IOT_OPS_INITIALIZED" ]; then
        echo "Initializing Azure IoT Operations on cluster '$RESOURCE_NAME'..."
        az iot ops init \
          --cluster "$RESOURCE_NAME" \
          --resource-group "$RESOURCE_GROUP" || {
            echo "ERROR: Failed to initialize Azure IoT Operations."
            final_status "FAILED" "Failed to initialize IoT Operations" \
              "Check 'az iot ops init' command output." \
              "Ensure cluster is Arc-connected and healthy." \
              "Check logs: $LOG_FILE"
            exit 1
          }
        echo "Azure IoT Operations initialized successfully."
      else
        echo "Azure IoT Operations namespace 'azure-iot-operations' already exists. Skipping init."
      fi

      ##### Step 12: Create IoT Ops instance #####
      # Get Schema Registry resource ID
      SR_ID=$(az iot ops schema registry show --name "$SCHEMA_REGISTRY" --resource-group "$RESOURCE_GROUP" --query id -o tsv)
      INSTANCE_NAME="${RESOURCE_NAME}-instance" # Instance name based on Arc resource name

      update_status "12" "Creating IoT Ops Instance" \
        "Command: az iot ops instance create" \
        "Instance Name:  $INSTANCE_NAME" \
        "Cluster:        $RESOURCE_NAME (Arc)" \
        "Resource Group: $RESOURCE_GROUP" \
        "Schema Reg ID:  $SR_ID" \
        "Profile:        Low memory (replicas=1, workers=1, rf=1)" \
        "This deploys Broker, etc. May take several minutes..." \
        "Track pods with: k9s"

      echo "Checking if IoT Ops instance '$INSTANCE_NAME' exists..."
       IOT_INSTANCE_EXISTS=$(az iot ops instance show --name "$INSTANCE_NAME" --resource-group "$RESOURCE_GROUP" --query name -o tsv 2>/dev/null)

      if [ -z "$IOT_INSTANCE_EXISTS" ]; then
        echo "Creating IoT Ops instance '$INSTANCE_NAME'..."
        az iot ops instance create \
          --cluster "$RESOURCE_NAME" \
          --resource-group "$RESOURCE_GROUP" \
          --name "$INSTANCE_NAME" \
          --sr-resource-id "$SR_ID" \
          --broker-frontend-replicas 1 \
          --broker-frontend-workers 1 \
          --broker-backend-part 1 \
          --broker-backend-workers 1 \
          --broker-backend-rf 1 \
          --broker-mem-profile Low || {
            echo "ERROR: Failed to create IoT Ops instance '$INSTANCE_NAME'."
             final_status "FAILED" "Failed to create IoT Ops instance" \
              "Check 'az iot ops instance create' command output." \
              "Ensure AIO was initialized correctly (Step 11)." \
              "Check prerequisite permissions." \
              "Check logs: $LOG_FILE"
            exit 1
          }
          echo "IoT Ops instance '$INSTANCE_NAME' creation initiated."
      else
        echo "IoT Ops instance '$INSTANCE_NAME' already exists. Skipping creation."
      fi

      update_status "12" "Waiting for IoT Ops pods" \
        "Checking pod status in all namespaces..." \
        "Waiting for all pods to be Running or Completed." \
        "This may take several minutes..." \
        "Track pods with: k9s" \
        "Track details: sudo tail -f $LOG_FILE"

      echo "Waiting for all Kubernetes pods to be Ready/Completed..."
      RETRIES=0
      MAX_RETRIES=20 # ~10 minutes (20 * 30s)
      PODS_READY=false
      while [ $RETRIES -lt $MAX_RETRIES ]; do
          # Get non-running/completed pods, excluding Evicted
          NON_READY_PODS=$(kubectl get pods -A --no-headers --field-selector=status.phase!=Succeeded,status.phase!=Failed | grep -v "Running.*1/1\|Running.*[2-9]/[2-9]\|Completed") # More robust check for readiness
          NUM_NON_READY=$(echo -n "$NON_READY_PODS" | grep -c '^') # Count lines accurately

          if [[ -z "$NON_READY_PODS" || "$NUM_NON_READY" -eq 0 ]]; then
              echo "All pods appear to be Running or Completed!"
              PODS_READY=true
              break
          fi

          echo "Waiting for pods to be ready... ($((RETRIES+1))/$MAX_RETRIES). Still waiting for:"
          # Provide slightly more info: NS, Name, Ready status, Status
          echo "$NON_READY_PODS" | awk '{printf "- %s/%s (%s, %s)\n", $1, $2, $3, $4}'
          RETRIES=$((RETRIES+1))

          if [ $RETRIES -eq $MAX_RETRIES ]; then
              echo "WARNING: Timed out waiting for all pods to become ready after $MAX_RETRIES attempts."
              echo "Please check the status of the following pods manually using 'kubectl get pods -A':"
              echo "$NON_READY_PODS"
              # Continue to final success message, but with a warning maybe?
              break # Exit loop, but don't fail the script entirely
          fi
          sleep 30
      done

      ##### Finalize #####
      echo "Performing final setup steps..."

      # Create workspace directory for the user
      if [ -d "$MYHOME" ]; then
        mkdir -p "$MYWORK"
        chown "$MYUSER:$MYUSER" "$MYWORK"
        echo "Created workspace directory: $MYWORK for user $MYUSER"
      fi

      # Final MOTD Status Update
      if $PODS_READY && $OVERALL_ASSIGNMENT_STATUS; then
        final_status "SETUP COMPLETE!" "Azure IoT Operations environment is ready." \
          "Resource Group:   $RESOURCE_GROUP" \
          "Arc K8s Resource: $RESOURCE_NAME" \
          "Storage Account:  $STORAGE_ACCOUNT" \
          "Schema Registry:  $SCHEMA_REGISTRY" \
          "IoT Ops Instance: $INSTANCE_NAME" \
          "" \
          "Useful commands:" \
          "kubectl get pods -A" \
          "kubectl get broker -A" \
          "k9s                (Kubernetes Terminal UI)" \
          "cd $MYWORK"
      else
        final_status "SETUP COMPLETED WITH WARNINGS" "Environment setup finished, but check warnings." \
          "Resource Group:   $RESOURCE_GROUP" \
          "Arc K8s Resource: $RESOURCE_NAME" \
          "Storage Account:  $STORAGE_ACCOUNT" \
          "Schema Registry:  $SCHEMA_REGISTRY" \
          "IoT Ops Instance: $INSTANCE_NAME" \
          "" \
          "Warnings encountered (check logs for details):" \
          $(! $PODS_READY && echo "- Pods not fully ready after timeout.") \
          $(! $OVERALL_ASSIGNMENT_STATUS && echo "- One or more role assignments failed.") \
          "" \
          "Review logs: sudo tail -f $LOG_FILE" \
          "Check pods: kubectl get pods -A"
      fi

      echo "========================================================"
      echo "Azure IoT Operations provisioning finished at $(date)"
      echo "Log file: ${LOG_FILE}"
      echo "Final Status: $(if $PODS_READY && $OVERALL_ASSIGNMENT_STATUS; then echo 'SUCCESS'; else echo 'COMPLETED WITH WARNINGS'; fi)"
      echo "========================================================"

      exit 0

  # 5. Run now script (for manual execution if needed)
  - path: /root/run_now.sh
    owner: root:root
    permissions: '0700'
    content: |
      #!/bin/bash
      echo "Starting Azure IoT Operations provisioning in background..."
      # Ensure script isn't already running
      if pgrep -f /root/provision_ops_vm.sh > /dev/null; then
          echo "Provisioning script appears to be already running. Check logs."
          exit 1
      fi
      LOG_TIMESTAMP=$(date +%F-%H%M)
      nohup bash /root/provision_ops_vm.sh &> "/var/log/manual-provision-${LOG_TIMESTAMP}.log" &
      PID=$!
      echo "Started provisioning script (PID: $PID) in background."
      echo "Monitor progress with:"
      echo "  watch cat /etc/motd"
      echo "  sudo tail -f /var/log/aio-provision.log"
      echo "  tail -f /var/log/manual-provision-${LOG_TIMESTAMP}.log"

  # 6. Systemd service file
  - path: /etc/systemd/system/aio-provision.service
    owner: root:root
    permissions: '0644'
    content: |
      [Unit]
      Description=Azure IoT Operations Provisioning Script
      Documentation=file:///root/provision_ops_vm.sh
      After=network-online.target docker.service
      Wants=network-online.target docker.service

      [Service]
      Type=simple
      User=root
      Group=root
      ExecStart=/bin/bash /root/provision_ops_vm.sh
      StandardOutput=journal+console
      StandardError=journal+console
      Restart=on-failure
      RestartSec=30s
      TimeoutStartSec=45m # Increased timeout slightly to 45 minutes

      [Install]
      WantedBy=multi-user.target

# Commands to run during boot, after files are written
runcmd:
  # Create necessary directories early
  - mkdir -p /etc/apt/keyrings
  - mkdir -p /root/.k9s
  - mkdir -p /var/log # Ensure log directory exists

  # Wait briefly for network/services to settle (optional, but can help)
  - sleep 20

  # Fetch Microsoft GPG key (used by azure-cli.list and packages-microsoft-prod.deb)
  - 'echo "Fetching Microsoft GPG key..."'
  - curl -sLS https://packages.microsoft.com/keys/microsoft.asc | gpg --dearmor | tee /etc/apt/keyrings/microsoft.gpg > /dev/null
  - chmod 644 /etc/apt/keyrings/microsoft.gpg # Ensure apt can read it

  # Reload systemd, enable and start the provisioning service
  - 'echo "Reloading systemd and starting provisioning service..."'
  - systemctl daemon-reload
  - systemctl enable aio-provision.service
  - systemctl start aio-provision.service
  - 'echo "aio-provision.service started. Check /etc/motd or logs for progress."'
